questions.stem:
A heated metal ball is dropped into a liquid. As the ball cools, its temperature, $T\,°\mathrm{C}$, $t$ minutes after it enters the liquid, is given by
$T = 400\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t}+25, \quad t \geqslant 0.$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the temperature of the ball as it enters the liquid.
(1)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the value of $t$ for which $T=300$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $300 = 400\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t}+25 \Rightarrow 400\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t} = 275$ sub. $T=300$ and attempt to rearrange to $\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t}=a$, where $a \in \mathbb{Q}$ M1
$\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t} = \frac{275}{400}$ A1
M1: correct application of logs
$t = 7.49$ A1 (4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the rate at which the temperature of the ball is decreasing at the instant when $t=50$. Give your answer in $°\mathrm{C}$ per minute to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\frac{dT}{dt} = -20\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t}$ (M1 for $k\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t}$) M1 A1
At $t=50$, rate of decrease $= (\pm)1.64\,°\mathrm{C/min}$ A1 (3)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) From the equation for temperature $T$ in terms of $t$, given above, explain why the temperature of the ball can never fall to $20\,°\mathrm{C}$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) $T>25$, (since $\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$) B1 (1)

questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows part of the curve with equation
$y = (2x-1)\tan 2x, \quad 0 \leqslant x < \frac{\pi}{4}.$
The curve has a minimum at the point $P$. The $x$-coordinate of $P$ is $k$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $k$ satisfies the equation
$4k+\sin 4k-2=0.$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Using product rule: $\frac{dy}{dx} = 2\tan 2x + 2(2x-1)\sec^2 2x$ M1 A1 A1
Use of "$\tan 2x = \frac{\sin 2x}{\cos 2x}$" and "$\sec 2x = \frac{1}{\cos 2x}$" M1
$[=2\frac{\sin 2x}{\cos 2x}+2(2x-1)\frac{1}{\cos^2 2x}]$
Setting $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$ and multiplying through to eliminate fractions M1
$[\Rightarrow 2\sin 2x\cos 2x + 2(2x-1)=0]$
Completion: producing $4k+\sin 4k-2=0$ with no wrong working seen and at least previous line seen. A1* (6)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The iterative formula
$x_{n+1} = \frac{1}{4}(2-\sin 4x_n), \quad x_0=0.3,$
is used to find an approximate value for $k$.
(b) Calculate the values of $x_1, x_2, x_3$ and $x_4$, giving your answers to 4 decimal places.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $x_1=0.2670$, $x_2=0.2809$, $x_3=0.2746$, $x_4=0.2774$, M1 A1 A1 (3)
Note: M1 for first correct application, first A1 for two correct, second A1 for all four correct
Max -1 deduction, if ALL correct to > 4 d.p. M1 A0 A1
SC: degree mode: M1 $x_1=0.4948$, A1 for $x_2=0.4948$, then A0; max 2

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Show that $k=0.277$, correct to 3 significant figures.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Choose suitable interval for $k$: e.g. $[0.2765,0.2775]$ and evaluate $\mathrm{f}(x)$ at these values M1
Show that $4k+\sin 4k-2$ changes sign and deduction A1 (2)
$[\mathrm{f}(0.2765)=-0.000087.., \mathrm{f}(0.2775)=+0.0057]$
Note: Continued iteration: (no marks in degree mode). Some evidence of further iterations leading to 0.2765 or better M1; Deduction A1

parts.text:
(a) Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta \equiv 1$, show that the $\mathrm{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta \equiv 1$.
